purpose: Challenge whether one finite storage-neutral current-link snapshot is sufficient for raw-pole deixis and a local equality/unification model without ContextFrame ontology, L4 realization, recursive graph-isomorphism equality or global rewriting.

currentLinkCarrier.current: one localRef inside the finite closed snapshot

localRefConstraint.meaning: after explicit local alias resolution, two already resolved semantic refs satisfy one atomic equality constraint iff their representatives are the same local ref

linkComparisonConcept.meaning: compare the two raw pole refs of A and B through local equality constraints

criticalDistinctions.virtualOccurrenceIdentityVsPairEquality: two distinct virtual node occurrences may have the same ordered pole refs; the link-comparison concept may classify them equal without globally merging their occurrence identities
criticalDistinctions.sameTopologyVsLocalEquality: two separately named recursive subgraphs that are merely isomorphic are not automatically equal when corresponding raw pole refs differ
criticalDistinctions.materializedExactPair: current L4 canonical exact-pair storage may map one ordered pair to one LinkRef; this is parity evidence, not the ontology of virtual links
criticalDistinctions.anonymousHole: occurrence-local [] remains a separate local unification mechanism and is not replaced by current-link deixis

candidateModels.summary: finite virtual current-link snapshot + raw destructors + local alias/identity constraints; link equality concept compares immediate pole representatives
automatically recurse through whole reachable graphs until isomorphism/bisimulation
candidateModels.problem: smuggles a much stronger external equality relation into one local = constraint and recreates issue #79 style global/meta assumptions

candidateModels.summary: ↑ must be a materialized L4 LinkRef
candidateModels.problem: violates virtual/read-only context and interpret != realize

challengeVectors: ordinary current X=(A,B) exposes A/B through one anchor
virtual and materialized representations with the same observable ordered poles give the same local raw-pole observations without asserting identity between representations
two virtual node occurrences with the same ordered pole refs can satisfy the derived link-comparison concept while remaining different occurrence refs
two merely isomorphic subgraphs with different corresponding local refs do not become equal by hidden recursion
explicit interpretation-local aliases may make corresponding pole refs equal without global mutation
current exact-pair L4 remains idempotent for materialized parity
no ContextFrame parent or hidden interpreter/session input is needed
no L4 write is performed by the virtual challenge
decisionQuestions: Can VirtualLinkSnapshot replace ContextFrame for local current-link observations?
Is local representative equality sufficient as the atomic = substrate for the derived link-comparison concept?
Do self/mutual cycles require any recursive equality mechanism beyond explicit local refs/aliases?
Does any required vector force ↑ to expose L4 identity?

releaseVeto.nextGateAfterChallenge: Gate E decision; equality remains candidate until the challenge evidence is classified
